summary: Wasco County lookout: L-6 tower built 1933, deactivated 1964, gone by 1967-69; only a couple of concrete pedestals remain, per a hiking guide.

facts.design: L-6 cab on a treated timber tower
facts.status_note: Tower gone by 1967-1969 depending on source (burned, removed or destroyed); only a couple of concrete pedestals remain per a hiking guide

access.note: On Mount Hood National Forest land; the hiking guide describes a walk from the site to a knoll with a Mount Hood view. No closure or private status appears in the sources

visit.trail_note: The site has no views; a walk north along the ridge on an old road track reaches a knoll cleared for a view of Mount Hood

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Mount Hood National Forest

events.note: 72-ft timber tower with L-6 cab, about $475 and 800 man-hours (Forest Lookouts); FFLOS and firelookout.com give 84 ft, built in the 1930s
Tower blown over in winter 1933-34 and re-erected in 1934
Staffed for one day by Ed Neubauer of the Trails Club of Oregon
Un-needed tower disposed of by burning (Forest Lookouts); hiking guide dates the tower to 1933-1967
FFLOS says removed about 1969; firelookout.com says destroyed about 1969
Registered on the Former Fire Lookout Sites register

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The brief's 21.9 m (72 ft) matches the 1933 build height in the Forest Lookouts history. The FFLOS register, firelookout.com and the hiking guide give 84 ft (25.6 m). The story gives both figures and facts uses 25.6 m.

resolved_conflicts.field: end date (burned 1967 vs removed or destroyed about 1969)
resolved_conflicts.explanation: Forest Lookouts says the tower was burned in 1967 and the hiking guide dates it to 1933-1967. The FFLOS register and firelookout.com say removed or destroyed about 1969. The story reports both.

notes_for_editor: Height and end date conflict across sources; the story gives both. Access 'public' is inferred from Mount Hood National Forest land and the hiking guide's route, not from a closure statement. The hiking guide shows no date in the fetched text. The brief's access 'unknown' is replaced. Brief's 21.9 m height is the 72 ft figure only.
